item.title: IDF: Over 2 million tons of food entered Gaza since ceasefire, prices down 72%
item.description: IDF details scope of humanitarian response in Gaza since October 2025 ceasefire, says some 600 trucks enter daily and hospital bed capacity has increased by more than 50%.

item.description: Karmei Oz and Sahlab received official locality codes, completing years-long recognition processes and enabling expanded services and development.

item.description: Justice Noam Sohlberg ruled that footage showing soldiers and an IDF artillery piece constitutes use of public assets and ordered Naftali Bennett to remove it.

item.title: Lebanon condemns Israeli strike on Syrian airbase
item.description:
The Lebanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants strongly condemned the Israeli airstrikes that targeted Abu al-Duhur Military Airport in Idlib Governorate on Tuesday. The Ministry stated that it considers these strikes a "blatant violation of the sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, as well as a clear breach of international law and the Charter of the United Nations."
The Ministry reaffirmed Lebanon's "firm support for Syria's sovereignty, security and stability, and stresses Lebanon's rejection of any attack on Syrian territory. It further underscores the need to put an end to these violations and refrain from any steps that could heighten tensions and threaten regional stability."

item.title: Ben-Gvir clashes with resident during visit to Bedouin Town
item.description: National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir clashed with a resident during a police tour of Basmat Tab'un, then praised a local driver's support for Israel.

item.title: Bereaved father: “Benayahu fell, but he left us a path that won't be stopped"
item.description: Boaz Melet tells Arutz Sheva how his son Benayahu, who was shot in a terrorist attack, recovered and continued fighting the terrorists until his final moments.

item.title: Central Elections Committee orders Together party to remove footage of troops from campaign video
item.description:
The chairman of the Central Elections Committee, Justice Noam Sohlberg, ordered Together party leader Naftali Bennett on Wednesday to remove footage of soldiers engaged in operational activity and an IDF artillery cannon from an election campaign video.
In the video, Bennett refers, among other things, to soldiers who have been fighting for months while Haredim evade military service. As he discusses the soldiers, the footage appears in the background. The Likud Party argued that this constituted the use of public assets and the IDF for election campaigning, in violation of the law.

item.title: IDF releases findings in 5 major Gaza incidents
item.description: IDF reviews examine WCK strike, deaths of Hind Rajab and MSF employees, and Tel al-Sultan incident; criminal investigations ordered in two of them.

item.title: Within less than 30 minutes: IDF eliminates two terrorists in Gaza
item.description: IDF strikes commander in Hamas' military wing who infiltrated Israel on October 7th. A short time later, the military eliminated a second commander who planned to attack IDF troops.

item.title: Zamir tours Syria after Israeli strike
item.description: IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir visits IDF positions in southern Syria following strike on Syrian airbase to prevent planned Turkish military deployment.

item.title: A debunked blood libel that keeps reappearing in an Israeli-based newspaper
item.description: A Jewish newspaper in Jerusalem propped up inflated charges of settler violence charges as unquestionably true, handing our declared enemies the one asset they cannot manufacture for themselves. Why does it continue to print the blood libel it has already debunked?

item.title: Bennett to Eisenkot: No exemptions, no deals
item.description: 'Together' chairman Naftali Bennett blasts 'Yashar!' chair Gadi Eisenkot's haredi draft plan and its 30% exemption proposal: 'We know exactly how it ends: with nothing.'

item.title: Glock, M16, and explosives seized in wave of raids
item.description: Israeli security forces uncovered firearms, ammunition, pipe bombs, and a hand grenade in a series of raids across Judea and Samaria, arresting a Palestinian man in his 50s.

item.title: Thousands of Breslov hasidim may be blocked from Uman
item.description: As the Jewish New Year approaches, rabbis weigh controversial plan to allow haredi draft evaders barred from leaving Israel to make the pilgrimage.

item.title: Karlin-Stolin Rebbe breaks silence after violent clashes
item.description: A day after extremists attacked his hasidim in Jerusalem, the Karlin-Stolin Rebbe praises their resolve, but warns 'use of force is not the way of the Torah.'

item.title: New AI platform brings Jewish tradition into the digital age
item.description: A new AI-powered platform launched in Savyon aims to make Jewish law, tradition and daily practices accessible worldwide, while connecting users with more than 1,000 rabbis.

item.title: IDF seals two Gaza terror tunnels
item.description: IDF troops seal over two kilometers of Hamas terror tunnels beneath Gaza, as operations to dismantle the terrorist organization's underground network continue.

item.title: Prison Service blocks MK's visit to jailed Gaza hospital chief
item.description: MK Ahmed Tibi was barred from meeting Dr. Hossam Abu Safiya after security officials warned the visit could pose a security risk.

item.title: Hamas-linked items found in Meah Shearim raid
item.description: Police searching two warehouses in Jerusalem neighborhood uncover PLO flags, anti-Israel material, incitement signs, and hat identified with Hamas.

item.title: Poll indicates Shas losing seats as Religious Zionist Party gains
item.description: New Kantar poll gives Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar! party 24 seats, narrowly ahead of Likud, while Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc falls short of a majority.

item.title: Chief of Staff finds new role for offcier blocked from promotion
item.description: Defense Minister Israel Katz rejected a promotion for Maj. Gen. Eliad Muati. Now, IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir has found a way to keep the senior officer in service.

item.title: Families wake up to bulldozers at their doors
item.description: Police forces raided Givat Ura Yisrael near Ariel, demolishing homes with belongings, religious books and children's items still inside.

item.title: Iran threatens US bases in Europe if war resumes
item.description: Sources close to Tehran tell the Financial Times Iran considering strikes on US assets in southeastern Europe, targeting undersea cables, if war renews.

item.title: Bereaved Mother: 'I never thought it would be the last hug'
item.description: The parents of Hillel Mordechai Dadon, the seven-and-a-half-year-old boy from Beit Shemesh who was brutally murdered by a neighbor, share their shock and grief at the incident.

item.description: Veteran Florida Democrat defeats crowded field after switching districts amid GOP-led redistricting effort, while facing criticism from Israel critics over her pro-Israel record.

item.title: Beware of Middle East Accords: They are regime-contingent
item.description: In the non-democratic Middle East, Islamic/Arab regimes do not ascend to power through the ballot. They tend to be tenuous, as are their policies and agreements, which are not anchored in democratic and legal structures, but in foundational Islamic precepts and precedents. An historical review.
